name: Crust
summary: The Moon's outer shell is about 40 km thick on the near side and about 60 km on the far side. The highlands crust is anorthosite; the far side kept a thicker crust, which is one reason it has so little volcanism.

name: Mantle
summary: Below the crust, the mantle is mostly olivine and pyroxene rock, and it is partly molten near the core. Impacts that dig deep enough can dredge mantle material up to the surface.

name: Liquid outer core
summary: A shell of liquid iron about 90 km thick wraps the solid inner core.

name: Solid inner core
summary: A ball of solid iron about 240 km in radius sits at the centre of the Moon.
